references.text: The same warning about the consequences of not obeying the Lord's commands and statutes, with a parallel structure regarding disobedience.
The warning about curses if the people do not obey the Lord's commands, containing the same thematic content about obedience to God's decrees.
The prophet Jeremiah notes that the fathers neither listened nor inclined their ears, but followed their own plans instead of obeying God.
The Lord warns against not listening to His law and not heeding His servants the prophets, addressing the same theme of failing to obey the Lord's word.
Ezekiel describes Israel's rebellion in Egypt where they refused to listen to the Lord, parallel to the warning about disobedience.
Joshua reminds the people that those who did not obey in the wilderness were not allowed to see the promised land, a consequence of disobedience.
Isaiah presents the same choice between obedience and blessing versus disobedience and judgment.
The continuation of the same passage describing the punishment for disobedience, directly contextualizing the verse.
A warning that Israel will perish if they do not listen to the Lord's voice, showing the same consequence of disobedience.
Samuel warns that the Lord's hand will be against the people if they do not obey His voice.
